text:
maria: quick idea — propose a "cohorted flag delegation" pattern for runtime config. allow product teams to own small cohorts (1%-10%) with delegated roll windows and TTLs so platform doesn’t need to babysit every rollout.

aj: curious, how do you see safety gates working?

maria: telemetry gating + automatic rollback. idea: each cohort rollout can point to a small metric bundle (error_rate, p95 latency, quality_eval_score). if any metric crosses threshold, system auto-teleports rollback and notifies owners.

lee: auto-rollback is 👏. we should also add a deadman timeout so if the delegation TTL expires we revert to platform default instead of leaving an orphaned flag.

maria: yup — TTL + owner contact required. delegation API would require: owner, cohort_percentage, ttl_seconds, metric_thresholds.

samir: frontend / console UX: show live cohort map, active traffic % per cohort, and a "preview in myorg" dry-run that applies rule only to my session. also one-click rollback and history diff.

aj: API shape idea (pseudo):
```json
POST /v1/flags/delegate
{
  "flag": "new-routing-v2",
  "cohort": "search-a-b",
  "owner": "product/search",
  "percent": 2,
  "ttl_seconds": 86400,
  "metrics": { "error_rate": 0.01, "p95_latency_ms": 600 }
}
```

lee: minor nit — nested metrics JSON in payload ok for docs, but make sure SDKs expose typed fields instead of freeform maps. also need an explainable resolution order (global < route < cohort override).

nora: from security/compliance: delegation requires audit log entry + signed acceptance by owner (email or SSO). also restrict delegations for flags that touch PII handling or billing.

console-service: +1 on audit and signed acceptance. we can add a console flow: request -> owner approval -> automatic probe dry-run -> promote.

maria: rollout policy sketch: phase 1: create cohort (dry-run, 0% actual traffic), phase 2: soft-sample (0.1%-2%), phase 3: ramp by metric checks until target percent, phase 4: promote to route or revert.

aj: two open questions: how do we surface partial failures (config apply succeeded but kernel route not found) and how to test boolean flags with multiple dependencies?

lee: for apply failures we should add an "apply_result" state and an exponential backoff retry queue + alert to owner after 3 fails. for dependent flags we can support simple prerequisites in config: `{ prerequisite_flags: ["A","B"], mode: "require_all" }` and surface unmet prerequisites in console.

maria: thinking about telemetry gating — we run a shadow evaluator that computes the quality_eval_score based on a canned prompt set. small cost but good safety net.

samir: can we show sample tokens/cases in console to quickly eyeball model outputs for the cohort? even 10 examples would help PMs.

maria: yes, include sample artifacts and diff view. also include cost-estimate delta for cohort (tokens, infra).

aj: operational concerns: need clear defaults for fail_open vs fail_closed. platform default should be fail_closed for risky flags, fail_open for UI experiments. classify flags via metadata.

nora: +1 on metadata classification — we need an allowlist for fail_open flags, and policy enforcement in private deployments.

ops-bot: scheduled reminder: run delegation safety audit for all active cohorts next Monday 09:00 UTC.

maria: next steps: (1) draft API contract, (2) wire audit + TTL enforcement, (3) console mockups for cohort map + rollback, (4) implement telemetry shadow pipeline. volunteer?

aj: i'll take API contract + SDK changes.

samir: i'll do console mockups.

lee: i'll own telemetry probe infra and apply_result state machine.

nora: i'll write the compliance checklist and the fail_open allowlist.

maria: awesome — i'll assemble a short RFC and timeline. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
